about: The home of Mojo, a new programming language for fast code, and Modular's tools for running AI models.

prs.title: Splitting text into lines no longer drops a line
prs.broken: When text mixed old-style Mac line breaks with normal ones, Mojo's split-into-lines function silently lost a line. "a, b, c" came back as "a, c".
prs.changed: I fixed a check meant to skip only empty pieces, so it no longer skips real lines.
prs.matters: Programs reading text from different systems get every line, the same as Python gives.

prs.title: Tests in a loop now check every round, not just the first
prs.broken: Mojo has a test helper that checks code crashes when it should. In a loop it re-ran the first round each time, so tests could pass having checked one case.
prs.changed: I made it count how many times each check has been reached, so every round runs its own case.
prs.matters: A test that reports a pass has now really checked every case it claims to.

prs.title: A stuck test now fails instead of hanging forever
prs.broken: Mojo's helper for testing deliberate crashes waited forever if the code froze instead of crashing. The whole test run stalled with no hint of which test was stuck.
prs.changed: I added a time limit, 60 seconds by default, after which it stops the stuck code and fails that test with its output.
prs.matters: Developers get a clear failure they can fix, instead of a frozen test run killed with no explanation.
